title: Need opinion: will this free indie vibecoder focused Gadot plugin help you?
author: Brotherindeed
selftext:
Greetings fellow game devs, i am not a game dev and this is my first game, been coding a while and have experience in writing shaders and i know some techniques that games often use but thats it, a normal programmer who cant code anymore because of vibecoding straight for a year and a half and not writing a single line myself.

  
so heres my workflow:  
**Deepseek v4.1 flash** (the only model i use for coding now)  
**Free assets** only from poly pizza (all of them from Quaternius this person has like 1400 low poly models for free basically and incredible packages too)  
**Stable Fast 3D** for generating assets i cant find for free online on my beaten up 7 year old gtx 1650 laptop  
**gadot** as the game engine (found it great for agentic game dev and the only game engine i know from like 4 years ago when i tried to make a game back then)

now here is what i did:  
1 discussed the idea out loud and decide the core gameplay loop, progression mechanics and theme  
2 downloaded assets from poly pizza (didn't start generating 3d assets just used generic models first, ideally rigged characters and simple houses etc)  
3 made a town and some basic terrain  
4 made a procedural way to generate towns (house from primitives, change your primitives designs and tweak the procedural generators variables to get a different feeling town)  
5 made npcs (with schedules and random variance along with a system to generate side quests)  
6 replace character and town primitives by generating them on stablefast 3d (verify every primitive visually, don't rely on llms for this, they mess up big time here)

now i guess unfolding the whole game is the next step maybe by making 2-4 towns on a small terrain and tie them together in a main quest (which in my system is simply a longer sidequest and shows up in the menu at the top)

i will not be selling the game, i will probably make it open source so anyone with a gtx 1650 laptop can make an actually playable game but thats not me which is kinda what i want help on.

i haven't nailed the combat, the story and many many more things.

i wanted to make a procedural game without being very artistic (bland artwork basically llms prompts sf3d, i only verify so the artwork works but is without a soul essentially)

so that later on someone can use the built procedural systems as a library so no one has to do this again, basically if you were to use my game as a plug and play library for making your own game then you could publish insane amounts of content as a solo artist without having to figure out realistic town generation or npc hangling for vibecoding a game and perhaps you can use the saved time to actually make the game more fun.

but there are just so damn many things in a simple 3d rpg, i took the chinese webnovel called reverend insanity (peak btw) as my game's inspiration.

its not a commercial game and ill use different names but the mechanics and the world is from reverand insanity, despite which you can easily use this to make a game set in the medieval or colonial eras or even scifi settings (not as plug and play for scifi cities but a very good starting point)

i wish for this project to help indie devs go from an idea to a large open world rpg with many unique feeling towns and a ton of sidequests is reduced to like a week, allowing them to theoretically focus more on game mechanics, art and how to make the game fun.  


now the actual question:  
now that i knoe how hard this actually is, i am starting to doubt the insane amount of work needed (at least 2 weeks) will this benefit anyone?

so either i would like some tips on how to get some of these mechanics premade in some free plugin (cc0 needed since this will also be cc0)  
or i would like your opinion on this system's worth to you as a free library, would it help you out or not?

anyways, apologies if this was impossible to read i am overworked and high.

comments.author: Cubey42
comments.body: After kind of glancing over this wall of text I'm still not even quite sure what the plug-in is. Just procedurally generated towns? I didn't think that's very hard to do already

replies.author: Brotherindeed
replies.body:
procedural terrain + procedural towns + procedural npcs with schedules (+ sidequest engine and randomness)   
and basically a whole easy to customise and use as base rpg game maybe?  
idk i just really wanted somoething like this too get started but never found it so there it was

replies.author: Cubey42
replies.body: well let me ask this, what does procedural mean in this instance? like a new world seed every time the player starts a game? just generated for the initial design? NPCs with schedules that generate random sidequests? its not really fleshed out or explained what exactly you're creating. Like sure these systems sound nice, but randomly generated content < curated created content.
